facts.fact: BusinessDay NG (2026-09-21) says Nigeria's five-year broadband strategy, the National Broadband Plan 2020-2025, has ended, and describes the next phase of broadband policy as still to come, without naming a successor plan.

BusinessDay NG says a committee led by Funke Opeke of MainOne, with Bashir Gwandu as co-chair, was inaugurated in December 2019 to develop a new five-year broadband strategy through 2025, which produced the National Broadband Plan 2020-2025.

BusinessDay NG, citing Nigerian Communications Commission data, reports broadband penetration of 51.97 percent in December 2025 against the plan's 70 percent target, and 4G at 52.95 percent of mobile subscriptions against the plan's 70 percent goal (target set for 2023).

BusinessDay NG says the NCC reported that the previous national broadband plan (2013-2018) exceeded its 30 percent penetration target, reaching 37.8 percent when the plan expired; the year of expiry is not given in the document beyond the plan's stated 2018 end.

facts.fact: BusinessDay NG (2020-09-17) refers to the 'recently updated Nigerian Broadband Plan' as an existing plan whose goals the ipNX-USTDA partnership will advance, and the NCC's Director of Technical Standards and Network Integrity says the grant is in line with the National Broadband Plan.

BusinessDay NG says a USTDA grant to ipNX, signed 2020-09-17 to expand fibre to more than 200,000 residences in Lagos, Abuja and Port Harcourt, is described by the US Ambassador as helping achieve the goals of the National Broadband Plan; the grant amount is not stated and the money is foreign, not a Nigerian budget line.

facts.fact: Nairametrics reports Nigeria's National Broadband Plan 2020-2025 expired in December 2025, four months before the article, though an NCC commissioner said the plan 'has not ended'.
NCC Executive Commissioner Abraham Oshadami said the regulator is reviewing the old plan's performance and is coming up with a new plan to succeed it.
The article sets NCC data of 51.97% broadband penetration (December 2025) against the plan's 70% target, and 52.95% of mobile subscriptions on 4G against its 70%-by-2023 milestone.

The Guardian reports that the second National Broadband Plan (2020-2025), with a 70 per cent broadband reach target, expires in two days, and NCC head Aminu Maida says engagement with the ministry on a third plan has begun.

ThisDay reports the Nigerian National Broadband Plan (2020-2025) had a December 2025 deadline for 70 per cent broadband penetration, which was missed, with penetration at 58.22 per cent in August 2026.

facts.fact: The Ministry's strategic blueprint (October 2023) says the National Broadband Plan was developed in line with the National Digital Economy Policy and that the Ministry will prioritise its review and implementation towards 70 percent broadband penetration by the end of 2025.

The VSAT policy states the Ministry developed a Nigerian National Broadband Policy (2020-2025), and ties the policy's aims to attaining the goals of the National Broadband Plan 2020-2025; it gives no adoption date, so its published date of 2021-03 is used.
